A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StructEval and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.4. Content can be matched reliably despite layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.2 report original evaluations of 12 LLMs, including aggregate and task-level results.

after.justification: The benchmark experiments are retained, and Section 2.1 adds a human audit of 397 sampled VQA pairs.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, two-pass review, output parsing, and weighted syntax, keyword, and VQA scoring procedures remain unchanged. The new human audit evaluates the existing framework without modifying its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,035 examples and 44 generation/conversion tasks. Appendix A.1 retains all formats, task mappings, and example counts; the audit samples existing VQA pairs.

E2.justification: v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 6 evaluate the same 12 models, and comparator membership also matches throughout Appendix A.2. GPT-4.1-mini remains the VQA judge.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an audit protocol involving expert fair/unfair judgments for 397 sampled VQA pairs and tabulation of judge correctness. Existing zero-shot prompts, decoding settings, hardware configuration, and benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 2.1 and new Table 3 add a targeted analysis of whether VQA questions are visually answerable and whether the judge answers them correctly. The earlier model-error and subtask-difficulty analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new audit supplies counts and accuracy proportions without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main and appendix benchmark scores and plotted results are unchanged, including GPT-4o's 76.02 and Qwen3-4B's 67.04 averages. v2 Table 3 adds reported fairness of 88.92% and judge accuracy of 98.30% on fair questions, although some table counts and totals are inconsistent.

T1.justification: The example, keyword, and VQA definitions and weighted scoring Equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. No new formal theory, derivation, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about model performance gaps and structured-generation difficulty. The audit adds supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v2 identifies visually inaccessible information as a source of unfair VQA questions and interprets high accuracy on fair questions as support for automated evaluation validity. The existing limitations concerning static interfaces and LLM-generated data remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The inference engines, parameters, RTX A6000 hardware, evaluation prompts, and Appendix A.4 generation prompt are retained. The existing project-page link moves into the abstract without a change in disclosed code or data access.

R1.justification: Section 5 retains the same prior-work comparisons and research positioning. The cited works match; expanded author lists and added bibliographic URLs concern existing references.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording corrections, adds figure cross-references and audit prose, updates affiliations and correspondence information, and adds an acknowledgement. Main sections, appendix organization, and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column presentation to a single-column journal layout throughout. Figure 1's panels are rearranged, v1 Figures 6 and 7 become panels 6a and 6b, new Table 3 is added, and figures and tables are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: The human audit provides a useful, limited check of VQA answerability and judge reliability that v1 lacked, while making evaluation weaknesses more explicit. Its benefit is reduced by sparse audit details and inconsistent Table 3 totals: 6 plus 347 equals 353, but the Correct total is 352. The retained benchmark evidence and this qualified validation support a modest overall improvement.
